requirements.text: A user should be able to enter a demo session.
A user should be able to inspect their accounts.
A user should be able to inspect their transaction history.
A user should be able to transfer funds between their own accounts.
A user should be able to view basic profile information.
The application must use only synthetic records.
The application must never initiate real payments.
The application must never connect to an external bank.
The target has one seeded demo customer.
The landing page provides a clearly labeled 'Enter Demo' action.
The 'Enter Demo' action opens the demo dashboard without requiring a password.
The 'Enter Demo' action opens the demo dashboard without requiring real identity information.
The header identifies the active demo customer.
The header provides a 'Log out' action.
Logging out returns the user to the landing page.
Protected dashboard views should not remain usable after logout.
Direct navigation to protected dashboard views after logout should return the user to the landing page or an access-required state.
Refreshing while in a valid demo session should preserve that session.
A logged-out user must not regain access merely by refreshing a protected page.
The dashboard shows the customer's checking account.
The dashboard shows the customer's savings account.
Each account displays a readable account name.
Each account displays a masked account identifier.
Each account displays account type.
Each account displays current available balance in USD.
Balances are displayed to two decimal places.
The UI must not expose a full account identifier.
Selecting an account opens an account detail view.
The account detail view shows the account's current balance.
The account detail view shows the account's related transaction history.
Account balances shown on the dashboard and detail view must agree with the latest successful transactions.
The user can transfer funds between the checking and savings accounts owned by the demo customer.
The transfer form includes a source account field.
The transfer form includes a destination account field.
The transfer form includes an amount field.
The transfer form includes an optional memo field.
The source and destination accounts for a transfer must be different.
Same-account transfers must be rejected with a clear explanation.
Same-account transfers must not alter balances.
Same-account transfers must not create a transaction.
The transfer amount must be a positive number greater than zero.
The transfer amount must have no more than two digits after the decimal point.
Blank transfer amount values must be rejected with a clear validation message.
Zero transfer amount values must be rejected with a clear validation message.
Negative transfer amount values must be rejected with a clear validation message.
Non-numeric transfer amount values must be rejected with a clear validation message.
Over-precision transfer amount values (more than two decimal places) must be rejected with a clear validation message.
Rejected input for transfer amount must not create a transaction.
Rejected input for transfer amount must not change balances.
The transfer amount must not exceed the source account's available balance.
If funds are insufficient, the transfer must be rejected.
If funds are insufficient, both balances must remain unchanged.
If funds are insufficient, no completed transfer must appear in history.
A valid transfer is atomic: the source balance decreases by the amount.
A valid transfer is atomic: the destination balance increases by the same amount.
No partial transfer is allowed.
A successful transfer creates one completed transfer record.
A successful transfer record can be found in both relevant account histories.
The transfer record shows the amount.
The transfer record shows the date and time.
The transfer record shows the source account.
The transfer record shows the destination account.
The transfer record shows the status.
The transfer record shows the memo if supplied.
The UI reports success only after the transfer has been committed.
If a transfer is rejected or fails, the UI must explain that it did not complete.
If a transfer is rejected or fails, the UI must not show a success state.
Refreshing after a successful transfer must preserve the updated balances.
Refreshing after a successful transfer must preserve the transaction record.
The user can view a combined transaction history.
The user can view account-specific history.
Each transaction history row shows date and time.
Each transaction history row shows description or memo.
Each transaction history row shows transaction type.
Each transaction history row shows amount.
Each transaction history row shows status.
Each transaction history row shows relevant account.
Amount direction should be clear for deposits.
Amount direction should be clear for withdrawals.
Amount direction should be clear for transfers.
The user can filter history by account.
The user can filter history by transaction type.
The user can filter history by status.
The user can filter history by date range.
When filters are applied, every displayed row must satisfy all selected filters.
The start and end dates for history filters are inclusive.
A transaction occurring on either boundary date must be included when it matches the other filters.
An empty result set must show a clear empty state.
An empty result set must not show an error.
An empty result set must not show unrelated transactions.
Clearing filters restores the unfiltered history.
A profile view displays only synthetic demo-customer details.
The profile view displays the demo-customer's display name.
The profile view displays the demo-customer's masked email address.
The profile view must not reveal passwords.
The profile view must not reveal authentication tokens.
The profile view must not reveal full account identifiers.
The profile view must not reveal data belonging to another user.
The target works in a current desktop browser.
The target works at a 1280 × 800 viewport.
The target remains usable at narrower widths than 1280x800.
Interactive controls have readable labels.
Interactive controls communicate loading states.
Interactive controls communicate success states.
Interactive controls communicate validation states.
Interactive controls communicate failure states.
A submitted action should not silently disappear.
While waiting for a submitted action, the UI should show a loading state.
While waiting for a submitted action, the UI should prevent accidental duplicate submission.
Navigation links and buttons lead to the labeled destination.
Navigation links and buttons perform the labeled action.
A recoverable error must leave the user able to retry.
A recoverable error must leave the user able to return to the dashboard.
The demo begins with enough historical transactions to exercise account filters.
The demo begins with enough historical transactions to exercise type filters.
The demo begins with enough historical transactions to exercise status filters.
The demo begins with enough historical transactions to exercise date filters.
Seed records should include multiple dates.
Seed records should include at least one transfer between the two accounts.
The demo has no signup features.
The demo has no external payment features.
The demo has no bill-pay features.
The demo has no loan features.
The demo has no card features.
The demo has no multi-user features.
